answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require each new identity to pass a signal challenge: complete a small, verifiable task that cannot be copied across accounts, then lock a modest deposit in a shared vault. A ferrous stamp, forged from the task proof and public history, marks its lineage, so duplicate stamps expose clones at once. Credit releases only after independent peers confirm the work; proven forgery forfeits the vault deposit and stains the lineage permanently. This raises the cost of mass fake identities while keeping entry affordable for honest newcomers.
